correctness.rationale: Exact conditional one-step identities for root-parent choice, change in total leaves and their product close the global and marked-event covariance recurrences. A positive homogeneous factor gives a closed solution, and a direct telescoping difference gives the strict gap at every positive reinforcement. Positive denominators and h are established for all relevant sizes; n=2 and deterministic first arrival are explicitly separated. Fixed-parameter Gamma products prove the asymptotic. The standalone proof checker independently enumerates complete parent histories (2–8 vertices, four rational reinforcement values) and verifies 2,777 exact assertions, including symbolic identities to size 59; enumeration is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural question in reinforced tree growth is how each individual root-attachment event predicts global terminal leaf abundance. The exact covariance gradient gives a structurally meaningful sharp boundary: zero reinforcement has equal contributions, while every positive reinforcement makes later arrivals strictly more associated with global leaves. The result is uniform across a full real-parameter family, closes the root-degree/leaf mixed moment, and quantifies the growth regime, rather than merely computing an arbitrary finite statistic.
